title: Content Brief
description: Atomic claims extracted from source documents, each with provenance. Slides are ASSEMBLED from claims rather than written from memory of the material. Two things fall out for free: you can prove no number was invented, and when a card turns out under-written you have a shelf of unused real rows to pull from instead of reaching for padding.

arc.description: Narrative sections in order, each naming the claim ids it draws on.

claims.description: Over-extract deliberately. A library of fifty cards needs far more than fifty claims, because the surplus is what resolves UNDERWRITTEN defects without inventing anything.

text.description: One assertion. If it needs 'and', it is two claims.

span.description: Line range or locator in the source, e.g. 'L412-418'

figure.description: The number, if this claim carries one. Veracity checks numbers against these.

weight.description: How central this is to the argument. Drives which claims get a whole card.

verbatim.description: True for quotes that must not be reworded

unused_pool.description: Claim ids not yet assigned to a card. The refiner draws from here to fix UNDERWRITTEN and SPARSE. When this empties, the answer is more extraction, not more spacing.
